resources.string: A rule files any transaction whose description contains a word you choose under a category you choose. Add one and it\'ll run on your next import.
Rules run top to bottom. The first one that matches wins.
Transactions it already categorised keep their categories. Only the rule goes.

plurals.name: rule_apply_body
plurals.item: This will recategorise %1$d transaction that already exists.
This will recategorise %1$d transactions that already exist.

plurals.name: rule_apply_locked_note
plurals.item: %1$d transaction you categorised yourself also matches. It will be skipped — rules never overwrite a category you chose.
%1$d transactions you categorised yourself also match. They will be skipped — rules never overwrite a category you chose.

resources.string: No existing transactions match. The rule is saved and will run on new imports.

plurals.name: rule_apply_nothing_locked_note
plurals.item: %1$d transaction matches, but you categorised it yourself, so it was left alone.
%1$d transactions match, but you categorised them yourself, so they were left alone.

resources.string: %1$d of the %2$d shown changed. The rest were locked or removed while this was open.
Matched anywhere in the transaction description, ignoring case. \"SWIGGY\" matches \"UPI/SWIGGY*ORDER/BANGALORE\".
Enter some text to match. A rule with nothing in it would match every transaction you have.
